title: The 30-Minute Attendance Chase No One Warned Me About
author: Anonymous Student
lead: Attendance became more about survival than learning.
body: Every morning felt like a race to avoid getting marked absent.
Even inside class, many students weren’t really learning.
Attendance anxiety is real, but it doesn’t define intelligence or growth.
College is often more about the stories we collect than the marks we receive.

title: Why I Stopped Following the Perfect Timeline
author: Anonymous Student
lead: I had my entire life planned out when I joined college.
body: But life didn’t follow the timeline I imagined.
Internships failed, grades slipped, and comparisons became exhausting.
Eventually I realized I’m not behind, I’m just on my own timeline.
Life feels lighter when you stop comparing your clock to someone else’s.

title: Hostel Nights and Heart-to-Hearts
author: Anonymous Student
lead: One sleepless hostel night turned into a deep conversation about fears and dreams.
body: We didn’t have solutions, but understanding each other made the future feel less scary.
Hostel life is not just about late-night snacks, but the heart-to-hearts that stay forever.

title: The Silent Battle with Self-Doubt
author: Anonymous Student
lead: The first week of college made me feel behind everyone else.
body: Every LinkedIn update or side project from others made me question myself.
Even when I achieved something, self-doubt whispered that it wasn’t enough.
People post their highlight reels, not their struggles.
Growth isn’t a race and confidence comes from progress, not comparison.
You’re not behind. You’re just on your own timeline.

title: Four Years In, I Still Don’t Know What I Want To Do.
author: Anonymous Student
lead: Everyone said college would give me clarity.
body: Four years later, I still don’t know what I’m actually meant to do.
We follow paths everyone says are safe while secretly wondering if they’re ours.
I have a degree, but no direction. A resume, but no real vision.
Maybe college shouldn’t just prepare us for jobs — it should help us prepare for life.

title: College Made Me Busy, Not Smart.
author: Anonymous Student
lead: Four semesters in, and all I’ve really learned is how to pull all-nighters and meet deadlines.
body: College feels more like checking boxes than real learning.
We attend classes, submit assignments, and prepare for endless tests.
But when I look at the real world, I don’t feel prepared or skilled — just tired.
We copy-paste code we don’t understand and memorize things we forget the next day.
All this work, but not much learning. All this busyness, but no real growth.
Maybe education should be more than a race to keep up.

title: I’ve Been in College 3 Years. I Still Don’t Know Anyone.
author: Anonymous Student
lead: Sometimes I wonder if people even know I exist on campus.
body: I’m in my third year of college, and honestly it feels like I never truly belonged here.
Everyone else seems to have their group while I just float around.
Classes feel transactional. Clubs feel cliquey. Group projects are silent WhatsApp chats.
Most days, it feels like I’m surrounded by people, yet completely alone.
No one warns you about this side of college — the loneliness and missing sense of community.
Maybe if colleges cared more about building connections, it wouldn’t feel this way.
Sometimes what students need most isn’t another lecture. It’s just someone to sit with.

title: Side Projects, Side Hustles, and the Side Effects of Hustle Culture
author: Anonymous Student
body: Start a side project.
Do an internship.
Build your LinkedIn profile.
At first, it feels exciting. Everyone is doing something extra: coding apps, freelancing, content creation, even running startups from their dorm rooms. And you feel like you should too.
But here’s what no one talks about: the side effects.

Some students stay up all night juggling projects, only to burn out before exams. Others compare themselves to peers and wonder, 'Am I doing enough?' Even when you achieve something, it rarely feels like enough because the hustle never ends.

Don’t get me wrong — side projects and hustles are amazing. They teach skills no classroom ever could. But the problem starts when hustle turns into pressure, curiosity turns into comparison, and passion turns into exhaustion.
After a few years of living in this cycle, here’s what I realized:
Productivity without balance becomes poison.
Not every hobby has to be monetized.
Sometimes, doing nothing is the most important project of all.
College is not a startup pitch deck. It’s a phase of life. And it’s okay if your biggest achievement some days is simply staying sane.
